reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a side-by-side analysis of Bittensor and NEAR, including protocol descriptions, market information, use cases, and comparative price data, while identifying the speaker's positive view of TAO as personal analysis rather than financial advice. The Bitunix registration link and requests to subscribe or engage are described as separate promotional or ordinary audience actions, with no stated reward, required payment, data request, deceptive condition, or connection to purchasing, investing, transferring money, or providing credentials.

opening.argument: The clearest solicitation pairs an earning claim with a registration destination: viewers are told to earn on Bitunix and given a register URL containing a referral code. That directs viewers toward an external account-opening flow while presenting earning as the reason to act. The surrounding discussion of TAO rewards and price performance gives the prompt a financial context, making it more persuasive than an unrelated link.

citations.quote: Earn on Bitunix Now 👉: https://www.bitunix.com/register?vipCode=cWec
receive TAO as rewards as a result of doing that

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the Bitunix link a separate promotion does not remove the promise-action pairing. The description puts “Earn” immediately before a registration URL containing a referral code. The video also discusses protocol rewards before directing viewers to that destination. No precise payout is needed to recognize an earning-oriented solicitation.

citations.quote: Earn on Bitunix Now 👉: https://www.bitunix.com/register?vipCode=cWec
All of these individual subnets get rewarded in TAO every single day.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Earn on Bitunix Now” does not specify what can be earned, how much, under what conditions, or whether registration itself produces any benefit. The supplied material shows a promotional link with a referral code, not a claim that viewers receive money or assets for registering. Discussion of TAO rewards concerns subnet contributors, not the audience’s Bitunix account.

opening.argument: The video combines crypto participation cues with strong appreciation framing. It says TAO outperformed NEAR by 246% in one year, describes Bittensor as having more potential, expects the uptrend to continue, and asks viewers which asset they hold. Those points spotlight past gains, future upside, and portfolio participation. Alongside the earning-registration link, the presentation can steer viewers toward acquiring or holding the favored asset without an equally prominent discussion of loss risk.

citations.quote: the past one year Tau has outperformed NIR by 246%
BitTensor has more potential than NIR protocol
I do think that will continue as we move through the rest of this cycle and beyond.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes historical data, but the speaker also states an upside view and predicts the uptrend will continue. The portfolio question invites the audience to consider holding these assets. Coupled with an earning-registration link, the progression from past returns to future potential and participation deserves scrutiny as promotion, not just abstract comparison.

citations.quote: BitTensor has more potential than NIR protocol
I do think that will continue as we move through the rest of this cycle and beyond.
Which one are you holding in your portfolio? Maybe you're holding both.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The 246% figure describes past relative price performance, not a promised future return. The speaker identifies the favorable view as personal opinion and says NEAR may also rise. Asking what viewers hold does not instruct them to buy TAO, and the earning link does not identify TAO acquisition as a condition. The evidence does not establish a deceptive purchase offer.

opening.argument: Although packaged as analysis, the video surrounds its financial discussion with external-action prompts. The description directs viewers to a crypto information page, Bitunix registration under an earning invitation, a free-book link, and a community link; the narration asks about viewers’ holdings. The comparison supplies credibility and attention for those prompts. Viewed together, the material functions as promotion that steers viewers toward an earning-branded registration flow, not solely as an educational comparison.
